title: Multimodal diffusion model generates future knee radiographs to forecast osteoarthritis
summary: KOA-Diff, a latent diffusion model fusing baseline X-rays, MRI and clinical data, was trained on the Osteoarthritis Initiative and tested externally on a private cohort of 80 knees. External binary Kellgren-Lawrence grade accuracy was 90.0% with joint space width error 2.06%, and in the Osteoarthritis Initiative accuracy was 84.0-91.8% over 96 months. Experts rated synthesized features about 3.9-4.2 out of 5, and model assistance raised clinicians' accuracy in identifying high-risk patients from 58.3% to 77.5%; the external cohort is small.
ai_technology: KOA-Diff latent diffusion model with multimodal fusion generating future knee radiographs

evidence.unknown: Performance in larger independent cohorts and effect on patient outcomes; full text not reviewed.
